subject: journey/nautilus
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. Inside the dry 1860s saloon of the Nautilus, a period wooden bellows plate camera on a wooden tripod is aimed directly out through a broad observation glass. Beyond the glass the ship’s electric lamp picks out bare black rock ridges on the deep ocean floor. No sunlight, no modern equipment.
